Department of Interior June 28, 1972
Page Thirteen
III. Safety and Operating Requirements -
While we are somewhat doubtful as to whether the National Environmental Policy Act gives the President and the Department legal authority to promulgate safety related requirements for ORRV use, the Association is not opposed to the imposition of reasonable regulations in this area. However, perhaps because of the absence of clear authority, the proposed safely related regulations are inequitable in that they impose the entire burden of compliance on the consumer although, in fairness, at least a portion of the compliance responsibility should rest on the vehicle manufacturer.
Moreover, a review of the proposed safety criteria indicates that they are not based on a careful consideration of the precise characteristics of the types of vehicles to be covered. As an example, consider the proposed requirement that persons operating ORRVs have valid permits to operate a motor vehicle. In the case of snowmobiles there is no demonstrated correlation between the ability to pass an automobile or motor-cycle drivers test and the ability to safely operate a snowmobile.
